A message from the Headteacher
Welcome to Chesham Grammar School, an outstanding, co-educational school of over 1300 students. CGS has a reputation for excellence. We have high academic standards and superb examination results.
Almost all of our students progress to their first choice university including Oxford and Cambridge. Our students will be the leaders of tomorrow and our aim is to ensure that they are well equipped for 21st century life. We want them to be confident, articulate and optimistic as well as respectful, tolerant and compassionate. Above all, we want them to be happy.

Latest News
what's happening at Chesham Grammar
CGS Spirit on Track for Sports Day
Throughout June, students in Years 7–10 and Year 12 proudly represented their houses in a range of track and field events as part of the annual Sports Day competition. The event culminated on the final Tuesday of June with an afternoon filled with colour, music, friendly competition and plenty of house spirit. The PE Department was delighted to see so many students taking part and giving their best.
Parents were welcomed to the event and enthusiastically cheered on competitors throughout the afternoon, with every participant contributing valuable points towards their house total. Congratulations to Franklin House, who secured the overall title for the third consecutive year.
A huge thank you goes to the PE Department and all the staff who helped organise and support the day. Special thanks also to Mr Madej, our resident DJ, who provided the soundtrack to the event (available on YouTube), and to Mrs Wynne, who beautifully captured the spirit and energy of the day through her artwork.

pageCache.text:
Latest News
what's happening at Chesham Grammar
Year 12 put their investigative skills to the test
Our Sociology and Psychology A level students took part in an immersive Murder Investigation Experience Day, following a case from an emergency 999 call through to a mock Crown Court trial.
Working alongside an experienced investigator, students gathered evidence, analysed forensic findings and examined suspects, applying their knowledge of criminology, law and investigative theory to practical tasks. The day concluded with a courtroom simulation, where students presented their findings and defended their decisions before a jury reached a verdict.
The experience provided valuable insight into careers in policing, forensic science, law and the wider criminal justice system, while also developing students’ confidence, teamwork and critical thinking skills.
A special thank you to Miss Fraser and Mrs Lovelace for organising this exciting opportunity.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Chesham Grammar School! I hope that our website gives you a clear insight into and understanding of life at CGS.
Ours is a vibrant school community, one of which we are very proud. It is characterised by a supportive and caring environment and relationships between staff and students are exceptionally warm. Visitors invariably comment on how welcoming, happy and friendly the school feels and this was commented on in our 2025 Ofsted inspection, which graded the school 'outstanding' in all areas.
Everything we do at CGS is underpinned by our vision and values. During their time with us, our students will be encouraged to aspire to excellence so that they can flourish and achieve their best in all that they do. We seek to develop a strong sense of belonging and our house system, central to the life of the school, plays a key part in this. We also want students to enjoy their time here. There is a very wide range of extra-curricular activities and opportunities available so that every student can participate in the wider life of the school. When students leave us, they are exceptionally well prepared for life and many of our alumni maintain close contact in their lives beyond CGS. This sense of community is very important to us.
Our staff are committed to achieving this shared purpose, whatever their role within the school. Teachers are innovative and creative, as well as passionate about their individual subject specialisation. This, along with our own distinctive CGS approach to learning ensures an inspiring and high-quality learning experience for all.
I hope the information you find here gives you a sense of life at Chesham Grammar School. Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to get in touch with us.
Annmarie McNaney Headteacher

Student Admissions
An introduction to Chesham Grammar School
11+ Admissions
Applications for admission to Chesham Grammar School at the start of Year 7 are handled by Buckinghamshire Council as part of its co-ordinated admissions scheme. If you are interested in making an application, please visit Buckinghamshire Council's website. All enquiries about 11+ admissions should be directed to the Admissions Team at Buckinghamshire Council.
Parents who live in Buckinghamshire will receive information about the 11+ process, through their primary school. Parents who live out of county, e.g. in Hertfordshire, London Boroughs, etc. should be aware that they need to register their child for the 11+ test at an earlier date. Further details can be found on Buckinghamshire Council's website.
If you would like to find out more about Chesham Grammar School, please contact us. We are always happy to answer any queries and will direct your question to the most appropriate person.
✉ office@cheshamgrammar.org
11+ Appeals
Our admissions appeals are handled, on our behalf, by Buckinghamshire Council. For information relating to appeals, please visit their website.
Admission of children with an EHCP into Year 7
Schools are required to admit a child where the school is named in Section I of an Education, Health & Care Plan. Before naming a school in an EHCP a Local Authority is required to consult with the school. Where a pupil is transferring from primary or middle school to secondary school, this consultation must be completed by 15 February in the calendar year of the transfer at the latest. Where CGS is consulted on being named in Section I of an EHCP, CGS will consider whether it would be unsuitable for the age, ability, aptitude or SEN of the child, and whether the attendance of the child there would be incompatible with the efficient education of others, and/or the efficient use of resources. The taking of the Buckinghamshire Secondary Transfer Test (STT) and obtaining of a qualifying score will be good evidence that the child is academically suited to the school.
EHCP consultations regarding a Buckinghamshire grammar school will therefore rarely be effective if the child has not yet sat or obtained their result from the STT. This is because CGS will not be able to respond to consultation effectively without knowing the academic ability of the child and what reasonable adjustments could be made, both of which are needed to inform the school’s assessment of suitability and compatibility with the education of others. For this reason, it is expected that all children seeking a place at CGS will take the STT and that their result is confirmed before the school is able to respond to an EHCP consultation.
The school will expect the local authority to follow this timetable in relation to consideration of naming the school in section I of a child's EHC Plan:
*For some children these dates may be later, e.g. because of illness on the day of the Test
Secondary Transfer Test 10 September 2026*
Results 9 October 2026*
Joining Chesham Grammar School in Years 8 and 9
Late Transfer Testing (entry to Year 8 and 9 September 2027)
Please note that CGS is currently full in all Key Stage 3 year groups. Pupils who qualify for a place as a result of late transfer testing will therefore be placed on a waiting list in accordance with our over subscription criteria in our Admissions Policy 2027.
Applications for admission into Years 8 and 9 are handled by Buckinghamshire Council as part of its co-ordinated admissions scheme. If you are interested in making an application, full details can be found on Buckinghamshire Council's website.
Our admissions appeals are handled, on our behalf, by Buckinghamshire Council. For information relating to appeals, please visit their website.
Year 10 Entry
Entry into Year 10 in September 2027
If you would like to apply for your child to be tested for a place in Year 10 in September 2027, please contact the school's admissions department from October 2026 onwards for an application form.
The deadline for registration for Year 10 entry tests is 31 January (or the next working day if that is a weekend) of the proposed year of entry, as stated in our Admissions Policy.
Sixth Form
Information relating to applications for our Sixth Form for September 2027 can be found in our Admissions Policy 2027.
The closing date for applications for admission to Year 12 in September 2027 is 04 December 2026.
The application form is available on the school's Applicaa website page.
Catchment Area
To check whether you live in catchment for CGS, please use Buckinghamshire Council's Find a secondary school near you tool.
A map of the school's Catchment Area can be found here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Leadership Team - Chesham Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Senior Leadership Team
Annmarie McNaney - Headteacher
Annmarie has been the Headteacher at CGS since September 2015. She joined the school as Head of Sixth Form in the late 90s before being promoted to Assistant Head and then Deputy Head, a role she held from January 2007 until her appointment as Headteacher. During her time on the Senior Leadership Team, she has introduced several new initiatives and was the driving force behind 'CGS Learning', the school's bespoke approach to teaching and learning. She was an integral part of the CGS journey from good to outstanding and is very proud of what was achieved in the process.
Before moving to Chesham Grammar, Annmarie taught at Backwell School, a large, nine form entry comprehensive school just outside Bristol, where she was Assistant Head of Sixth Form. Annmarie is a graduate of the University of Bristol where she read Theology and Sociology and where she also studied for her PGCE. Annmarie lives in Berkhamsted and is married with two sons, both of whom joined CGS in Year 7. Both sons are now CGS alumni, the elder leaving in 2021, going on to a Degree Apprenticeship with UBS. The younger, a member of our Class of 2024, is now at Manchester University reading Economics.
Tim Patteson - Deputy Head
Tim joined Chesham Grammar School in September 2015 having been Subject Leader of Geography at Dr Challoner's Grammar School, Amersham for four years. Prior to that, he worked at Sir John Lawes School, a mixed comprehensive in Harpenden. His current role includes responsibility for teaching and learning as well as staff professional development. He is married with two young daughters and two sons.
Hugh Bradbury - Assistant Head
Hugh joined CGS in 2012. Prior to becoming Assistant Head, Hugh was Subject Leader for History and before that, led the Politics Department. Hugh has performed a number of other roles within and beyond the school as More Able and Talented Coordinator and also as a Specialist Leader for Education for the ASTRA Alliance. Within that role he worked closely with the ASTRA SCITT, in particular delivering the subject specific training to History trainees from across the Alliance. His primary teaching subjects at CGS are History and Politics and his main responsibilities as Assistant Head are overseeing pastoral care and supporting the wellbeing of students as the Designated Safeguarding Lead, Designated Mental Health Lead and SENDCO. Hugh also continues to work with ASTRA helping to facilitate the National Professional Qualification for SENDCOs. Hugh grew up in Sussex and Surrey and then went on to complete his undergraduate degree and teacher training at the University of Exeter. He now lives in Chesham.
Sebastian Hayes - Assistant Head
Seb joined CGS in 2018 as Subject Leader for History. Seb started his working career on the John Lewis Graduate Development programme before changing careers and completing his teacher training at UCL. Seb worked as Head of History in London and taught in Madrid before joining CGS.
In 2020 Seb took on the role of Associate Assistant Head and led the school's work on recovery following the pandemic. In 2021 he joined the team in an acting capacity before taking up a permanent position in September 2023. In his substantive role he leads on Teaching and Learning, Character Education and Student Leadership.
Simon Pearce - Assistant Head
Simon joined CGS in September 2024, taking on the role of Assistant Headteacher with responsiblity for Data, Assessment and Digital Strategy.
Before joining CGS, Simon worked at Beaconsfield High School for five years in a number of capacities including Head of Science, ITTCo and ECF Professional Tutor and Acting Assistant Headteacher. Simon has previously held roles as Head of Chemistry and as KS5 Head of Year in schools in London and Madrid.
Simon grew up near Watford, before attending Bristol University to study Chemistry. He now lives in Chesham with his wife and two children.
Kevin joined CGS in 2013 as Team Leader for Science, after working for 11 years in schools in Yorkshire, the Midlands and more recently in Berkshire. Kevin's primary subject is Biology, he also has experience of teaching the other Sciences to KS4 and PSE. Kevin is the Educational Visits Coordinator at CG. His other responsibilities include overseeing attendance, the school calendar, and staff appraisal. Kevin lives in High Wycombe with his wife and young daughter.
Sarah Hammond - Finance and Operations Director
Sarah joined Chesham Grammar School in July 2021 as the Schools Finance and Operations Director, having worked in similar roles in a number of Buckinghamshire schools that faced very different financial challenges. Sarah has extensive Local Government finance experience and previously was Director of Finance and Resources for two large local authority housing organisations. She is a qualified accountant and has for a number of years been a governor in a local junior school. Sarah is married with two daughters and spends her free time managing the Girls Rugby Section at Chesham Rugby Club.
Marion Rasekh - Associate Assistant Headteacher
Marion joined CGS in 2016. Prior to this, Marion worked in south east London, leading departments in Religious Studies, Politics, and PSHE Education, as well as serving in pastoral leadership. She also had the enriching experience of teaching in Japan for three years.
Marion currently serves as Subject Leader for Life Skills and a Year Leader, while also fulfilling her responsibilities as Associate Assistant Head, where she takes the lead on equality, diversity, inclusion (EDI) and wellbeing. Marion grew up in the Wirral and she studied Sociology and Religious Studies at Gloucestershire University. Today, she calls Pitstone home, where she resides with her husband and two children.

pageCache.pageTitle: Student Absence Notification - Chesham Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Student Absence Notification
Attendance Officer
absence@cheshamgrammar.org
Tel: 01494 782854 (option 1) or DD: 01494 218130
On the Day Absence
Parents/Carers should notify the school of a child's absence via their MCAS (MyChildAtSchool) account (select Attendance > Report an absence from the dashboard).
If you are unable to do so via MCAS, please notify the school by telephone or email before 08:45 stating clearly the reason for absence, with Student Name, Tutor Group and Year Group.
In the case of illness, please contact the school every morning of absence confirming symptoms for our records.
Should a child feel unwell during the course of the school day, they should speak to their teacher in the first instance if they are in a lesson, or go to see Matron. Students should not call home to be collected. Matron will make contact, if necessary, following assessment.
Future Absence
Please, where possible, make medical or dental appointments outside of school hours.
For medical or dental appointments or assessments, and external exams (e.g. ABRSM, LAMDA, university entrance exams, driving tests) within school hours, university visits or work experience placements (Sixth Form only), please notify the school of your child's absence in advance, via MCAS.
It is expected that students will attend school prior to and after any such appointment in order to minimise absence from lessons. Students must be met at school by parents when leaving for an appointment and should sign out and back in with the Attendance Officer on their return.
All Other Absences
A Leave of Absence Application to the Headteacher should be completed, in advance, for absence for holidays or family events, etc.
Please refer to our Attendance Policy and Procedures for further information.

Careers Programme
Chesham Grammar School:
Committed to maintaining the Quality in Careers standard and proud holders of the Investor in Careers Award.
CGS Careers Office:
Helping to inspire, educate, inform, advise and guide our students into success after CGS
Careers and Enterprise Leader:
✉ Kate Lovelace or ✉ CGS Careers Office
The Careers Policy and the Provider Access Policy can be found here.
Careers Education, Information, Advice & Guidance (CEIAG)
CGS is committed to providing high quality impartial careers education, information, advice and guidance support to all students and holds the Investor in Careers Quality Award, for which it is re-assessed every three years.
Our Careers programme takes the form of a structured programme of learning which is integrated into the school curriculum through subject lessons, Life skills lessons, and during off-timetable careers events. The overall aim of the programme is to prepare students for the challenges and opportunities of adult life by:
What is the Careers Education Programme?
All students in Years 7-11 have dedicated careers lessons as part of the Life Skills programme. Student feedback helps inform the content of lessons which are also designed to address the learning outcomes of the CDi (Career Development Institute) Framework for careers education.
In the Sixth Form, students attend a carefully planned series of lectures and workshops which are tailored to the needs and interest of our students and also address the learning outcomes of the KS5 CDi Framework for careers education.
Where can you find support in school?
General Careers Support
Mrs Lovelace manages the school's careers programme which is intended to help to inspire, educate, inform, advise and guide all students into success after CGS. All students are welcome to visit the Careers Office at any time to speak to her about any aspect of careers or transition support (e.g. choosing options subjects, apprenticeships etc) or for support with work experience or work shadowing.
Mrs Lovelace also manages the careers library (in the careers office) where students will find up to date college and university prospectuses, apprenticeship information, gap year and volunteering opportunities along with many different career books and periodicals and other general careers information. Students can come to the careers office for careers-related research at break and lunchtimes.
Students and parents can also follow careers related information and opportunities on our social media accounts.
UCAS and References
UCAS
For specific questions about UCAS or university applications, Sixth Form students should first speak to Mr Wescomb (Director of Sixth Form) or Mrs Griffin (Post 18 Co-ordinator) in the Sixth Form Office.
References
All CGS staff are committed to supporting students to achieve their full potential and realise their aspirations. Tutors know their tutees well and support students with applications where appropriate.
What about independent advice and guidance?
CGS is committed to providing impartial information and advice at all times. CGS retains the services of an independent careers advisor who gives regular impartial advice and guidance to all students. Please request an appointment via the â CGS Careers Office
The Careers Adviser is in school on a regular basis. All Year 11 and Year 12 students will meet the adviser in small groups as part of their Post-16 & Post-18 Options process. One to one interviews are available on request for any students in Year 7-13, please see Mrs Lovelace.
Alternatively the National Careers Service offers free impartial careers advice with a qualified advisor.
What support is provided for transition?
The careers programme includes a number of focussed events to support transition.
Work Experience
Work shadowing: Parents of Year 8 students are encouraged to participate in a “take your child to work day.”
Work experience: Year 11 students are encouraged to undertake work experience after GCSE exams.
Work experience is also an integral part of the Sixth Form programme in Year 12 or Year 13.
Year 11 and Year 12 Work experience:
We strongly encourage all students to undertake work experience after their GCSE examinations (if they are 16 years old) and during Year 12. This is a parent/child arranged work experience, where students and parents take responsibility for organising the placement and responsibility for the duty of care of the student whilst on placement.
Students are asked to log their work shadowing and work experience on Unifrog. Parents are asked to inform the school by completing an online form (sent via email) with details of any arranged work placements. This form can also be used to inform the school of any voluntary work.
Year 11 Work experience assembly
What other support is provided?
All students are strongly encouraged to engage with as many opportunities as possible to broaden their knowledge of the world of work and careers during their time at CGS. The Careers Leader provides access to a very wide variety of opportunities for students via internal school communications and on social media.
Careers Fair
Every two years there is a CGS Careers Fair which is open to all students and typically has over 100 FE, HE, apprenticeship and career-specific exhibitors: Careers Fair Brochure 2025.
Careers Programme
Please see our CGS Careers Programme for full details about our programme. The Careers Programme is reviewed annually in the Summer Term by the Careers Leader. The COMPASS self-evaluation tool along with student/parental questionnaires and student destinations are used to evaluate the programme's impact on our students.
